advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Tighten the over-length size assertion to the send path's actual ADF budget (fit-outbound fixed point on the serialized wire) instead of the looser 32767 differ limit.
evidence: test asserts: `assert len(body_arg) <= _JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS` with `_JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS = 32767` (test lines 22, 88-90), and `body_arg` is the serialized ADF `json.dumps(codec.to_wire(...))`
acli_cli_ops build: `body_arg = json.dumps(codec.to_wire(fit_preserving_marker(body, codec.fit_outbound)))` with `codec = AdfCodec(rich="cloud" in cutover_clients())`
adf.py:332 `_ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT: int = 32000` and adf.py:341-363 fits the serialized ADF to that limit — so the real guarantee on `body_arg` is <= 32000, not <= 32767
ticket 5931 comment: 'the differ fits at `_JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS` while the send path fits at the 32000 ADF limit' — the 32000/32767 gap is a live, filed divergence (e339-9709-15fe-419a)
advisory.finding: The over-length size-contract assertion uses a bound (32767) that is 767 chars looser than the send path's actual guarantee. The real Cloud comment fitter is `AdfCodec(rich=False).fit_outbound` -> `adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit`, which fits the SERIALIZED ADF to `_ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT = 32000`, but the test asserts only `len(body_arg) <= _JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS` (32767) on the serialized ADF. A regression that let the serialized body grow into the (32000, 32767] window would pass this test even though it violates the ADF send-path budget the comment describes as broken.
scenarios: A future change alters the ADF fitter budget or reintroduces the 32767 differ limit on the send path; serialized ADF lands between 32001 and 32767; this test still passes.
The comment claims 'the existing size contract is not broken' but the assertion cannot detect a break of the actual 32000 send-path budget.
advisory.suggested_fix: Assert the send path's real guarantee rather than a raw char bound, e.g. `assert body_arg == json.dumps(AdfCodec(rich=False).to_wire(AdfCodec(rich=False).fit_outbound(landed_content)))` or assert the serialized ADF is a fixed point of the fitter (`codec.fit_outbound` idempotence), which pins the 32000 ADF budget directly and is refactor-safe.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the `best is None` fallback still emits a marked body (or documents why it is unreachable for the real Jira budget).
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_comments.py:280: `    return best if best is not None else probe`
`probe = fit(text)` truncates from the RIGHT and thus drops the marker (the function's own stated failure mode)
ABSENCE: no test exercises the `best is None` branch; a body where even `_decorate_outbound_comment('' + notice)` overflows the limit would land unmarked and be re-mirrored
dropped.finding: In fit_preserving_marker the pathological fallback returns `probe`, which is the vendor fitter's own truncated output with the RECONCILER_MARKER already cut off — reintroducing the exact unmarked-echo bug this function exists to prevent whenever even the bare decoration exceeds the limit.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive the vendor notice robustly (e.g. from the known suffix contract or a probe that cannot alias content) rather than a raw common-prefix diff that can overshoot on a matching boundary character.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/adf.py:333: `_ADF_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX: str = " … [truncated by reconciler]"` (notice begins with a space)
The fitter yields `probe = text[:m] + suffix`; if `text[m] == ' '` the prefix scan continues into the suffix, so `notice` loses leading characters
ABSENCE: tests only use `'x'*N` content, where `text[m]=='x'` never matches the notice's leading space, so this path is unexercised
dropped.finding: The truncation notice is reconstructed as `probe[len(_common_prefix(text, probe)):]`, but the common-prefix scan can overshoot the true cut point when the original character at the cut boundary equals the notice's leading character (a space), producing a truncated/incorrect notice string that is then re-appended to the rebuilt body.
